narrativeReportMd:
# Organization R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Local breaking changes are present. The largest R4-to-R6 breaks are the removal of top-level `Organization.telecom` and `Organization.address`, and the remodel of `Organization.contact` from a local backbone to `ExtendedContactDetail`. R6 also adds new optional `description` and `qualification` content that creates R6-to-R4 round-trip risk.

## Scope
I compared the R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions for `Organization`, package indexes, package metadata, and supporting definitions needed to understand local Organization changes. I excluded inherited Resource/DomainResource/DataType changes and treated Organization SearchParameters as separate artifacts.

## Main migration themes
The resource moves official contact details into `Organization.contact`, so existing direct `telecom` and `address` data must be structurally transformed. Contact code must be regenerated or adapted because `Organization.contact` is now `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `contact.name` changes from a singleton object to a repeating array. R6 adds richer descriptive and qualification data that cannot be represented losslessly in base R4.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `Organization.telecom` removal, `Organization.address` removal, and the `Organization.contact` type/serialization remodel. The `Organization.qualification` addition is high impact for R6-to-R4 downgrade rather than R4-to-R6 validation.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for contact grouping/downgrade policy and for qualification mappings, especially where accreditation or licensure data drives eligibility or directory trust.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most forward breaks could have been softened by retaining deprecated aliases for one release, but the R6 design appears to favor a unified, reusable official-contact model. Optional additions are forward-compatible but still need explicit downgrade policy.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should examine `ExtendedContactDetail`, Organization SearchParameters, base Resource/DomainResource changes, and external terminology expansions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Organization has material local breaking changes. Top-level `telecom` and `address` are removed, `contact` is remodeled through `ExtendedContactDetail`, and R6-only `description`/`qualification` content needs downgrade policy. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas, with terminology-expansion and official-diff limitations.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly structural: move official telecom/address data into `contact`, update generated code for `ExtendedContactDetail`, convert `contact.name` to an array, and define R6-to-R4 extension or loss policy for `description`, contact period/organization, and `qualification`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because the assigned R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are present and the local element deltas are explicit in the snapshots/differentials. Confidence is lower for terminology code-level impact and rationale because official diffs, narrative migration notes, and terminology expansions were not supplied.

findings.title: Top-level Organization.telecom was removed and folded into Organization.contact.telecom

oldState.summary: R4 had a top-level `Organization.telecom` element, `0..* ContactPoint`.

constraints.human: The telecom of an organization can never be of use 'home'

semanticText.short: A contact detail for the organization
semanticText.definition: A contact detail for the organization.
semanticText.comment: The use code 'home' is not to be used. Note that these contacts are not the contact details of people who are employed by or represent the organization, but official contacts for the organization itself.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Organization.telecom` carried official organization phone, email, fax, URL, and similar contact points directly under the resource.

newState.summary: R6 no longer defines top-level `Organization.telecom`; official telecom data is represented under repeated `Organization.contact` entries of type `ExtendedContactDetail`.

constraints.human: The telecom of an organization can never be of use 'home'

semanticText.short: Official contact details for the Organization
semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available relevant to the specific Organization. This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.

newState.narrativeMd: `Organization.contact.telecom` is available through the `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype, but the old top-level JSON property is not part of the R6 resource shape.

facts.note: No R6 local element with this id/path exists.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 comments describe `Organization.telecom` as official organization contact data. The R6 `Organization.contact` definition explicitly covers official communication devices including phone, fax, mobile, email, and web sites, and its datatype contains `telecom 0..* ContactPoint`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and validation break. An R4 instance containing the top-level `telecom` array uses an element that is absent from the R6 `Organization` content model, so strict R6 parsers and validators will reject it unless it is transformed into `contact.telecom`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Official phone, email, and web contact details are common directory data. Dropping or failing to migrate them can break patient, provider, payer, and administrative communication workflows.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 consolidates official organization contact data into `ExtendedContactDetail`, where telecom can be grouped with purpose, address, period, and handling organization context. A deprecated top-level alias could have softened the wire-format break, but it would leave two base locations for the same official telecom facts. Because that duplication creates material interoperability and lifecycle tradeoffs, the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.inferredGoal: Unify organization contact details under `ExtendedContactDetail` so communication channels, addresses, purposes, periods, and handling organizations can be represented consistently.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated top-level `Organization.telecom` while adding `Organization.contact.telecom` and normalization guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept `Organization.telecom` as `0..* ContactPoint`, marked it deprecated, and introduced `Organization.contact.telecom` as the preferred representation. Existing R4 instances would then continue to validate. The tradeoff is substantial: servers, validators, search parameters, and update logic would need rules for duplicate or conflicting telecom data, and the deprecated representation might persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 instances, but creates duplicate official-telecom locations with persistent ambiguity for validation, search, and updates.

evidence.quote: A contact detail for the organization.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `Organization.contact` as `0..* ExtendedContactDetail` and no longer has `Organization.telecom`.
evidence.quote: Official contact details for the Organization

examples.examplesMd: The fragments focus on the changed element and include `name` so the unchanged `org-1` invariant is satisfied.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the direct `Organization.telecom` array. Existing R4 data with official organization phone, email, fax, or URL values must be wrapped in one or more `Organization.contact` entries. This affects both validators and generated client/server models because the property moves from a direct resource field to a child of a complex contact datatype.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `Organization.telecom` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 because the element is no longer allowed at the top level. R6 contact telecom data can usually be mapped back to some R4 contact representation, but context such as R6 contact period or handler organization may not survive a simple downgrade.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move each top-level `telecom` item into `Organization.contact.telecom`. If the source system already has purpose-specific contacts, decide whether to merge telecoms into existing contact entries or create separate entries. Regression tests should include organizations with several telecom systems and uses, including the prohibited `home` use.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation is understandable, but not fully backward-compatible. A transition period with both a deprecated top-level element and the new contact structure would have allowed old instances to validate while encouraging migration.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 exposed `Organization.telecom` as a top-level repeating `ContactPoint` for official organization contact details, with an error rule excluding `home` use. R6 removes that path and expects official telecom values to appear under `Organization.contact.telecom` through `ExtendedContactDetail`. An R4 directory Organization with a phone, email, fax, or website at the old path is therefore old-valid/new-invalid until transformed, and generated models lose a familiar common property. The migration is not conceptually hard, but this is a common directory field on a mature trial-use resource, so the direct wire-format break looks large enough to deserve renewed design attention.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Organization.telecom` is `0..* ContactPoint`, official organization contact detail, and forbids `use = home`.
R6 StructureDefinition: no `Organization.telecom`; `Organization.contact` is `0..* ExtendedContactDetail` for official contact details.
R6 ExtendedContactDetail: `telecom` is `0..* ContactPoint`.
R4 maturity map: Organization is FMM 3, standards status trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the compatibility concern for a common path, but less than a normative/FMM 5 resource. I did not use the R6 normative status to increase the R4 compatibility burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing top-level `telecom` are not valid against the R6 Organization content model, with related runtime/API/codegen churn for generated `telecom` properties.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design could have retained `Organization.telecom` as a deprecated transitional alias while introducing `Organization.contact.telecom`. That would preserve most R4 instances, but it would create duplicate places for official telecom data and require conflict, search, and update rules. The tradeoff is real, yet the alternative is plausible enough for a common FMM 3 field to merit reconsideration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing high impact and partial-alternative assessment: the hard break and migration target are real, but I judge the common mature field plus plausible transitional alias as warranting Revisit rather than simply accepting the break as probably justified.

findings.title: Top-level Organization.address was removed and folded into Organization.contact.address

oldState.summary: R4 had a top-level `Organization.address` element, `0..* Address`.

constraints.human: An address of an organization can never be of use 'home'

semanticText.comment: Organization may have multiple addresses with different uses or applicable periods. The use code 'home' is not to be used.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Organization.address` represented postal, physical, billing, and similar organization addresses directly under the resource.

newState.summary: R6 no longer defines top-level `Organization.address`; address data is represented as `Organization.contact.address` through `ExtendedContactDetail`.

constraints.human: The address of an organization can never be of use 'home'

semanticText.short: Official contact details for the Organization
semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available relevant to the specific Organization. This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.

newState.narrativeMd: `ExtendedContactDetail.address` is `0..1` per contact entry, so multiple R4 top-level addresses generally become multiple R6 contact entries unless they can be grouped with other contact details.

facts.note: No R6 local element with this id/path exists.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `Organization.contact` text expressly includes addresses as official organization contact details, and `ExtendedContactDetail.address` supplies the address slot.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for R4 instances that carry `Organization.address`. Strict R6 validation will reject the top-level array, and generated R6 models will not expose that property.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Organization addresses are common for directories, billing, reporting, routing, and identity disambiguation. Failed migration can cause operational misrouting or directory quality issues.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of treating organization addresses as official contact details is coherent, especially because `ExtendedContactDetail` can group an address with purpose, telecom, period, and handler context. Keeping the old top-level address would avoid much R4 validation breakage, but it would also preserve a competing same-resource representation for the same address facts. That material duplication makes the R6 break probably justified, though not unavoidable in a narrow technical sense.
justification.inferredGoal: Represent addresses as purpose-specific official contact details rather than as a separate top-level collection.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated top-level `Organization.address` while adding `Organization.contact.address` and explicit grouping/search rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept `Organization.address 0..*` as deprecated and added `Organization.contact.address` for the new contact model. This would preserve old R4 JSON, but implementers would need to decide whether top-level and contact addresses are duplicates or distinct contacts, how to apply the no-home invariant, and how address search should index both locations. The risk is that both representations remain permanently active.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 address instances, but duplicates address-bearing fields and complicates grouping, search indexing, and conflict handling.

evidence.detail: R6 defines official contact details through `Organization.contact` and has no top-level `Organization.address` element.
evidence.quote: This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.

examples.examplesMd: For multiple R4 addresses, a lossless R6 transform typically creates multiple `contact` entries or groups each address with matching purpose/telecom context when available.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the direct `Organization.address` array. This is a high-impact migration concern because organization addresses are common and often indexed. Implementers must transform addresses into the new official contact structure rather than simply changing validation version.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with top-level `address` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6. R6 can carry equivalent address values, but the structural location and grouping rules changed, and each `ExtendedContactDetail` has at most one address.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move each top-level R4 address into an `Organization.contact` entry. Preserve `Address.use`, periods, lines, and jurisdictional details. If downstream systems depend on address search, rebuild indexes against the R6 contact-address path; the SearchParameter artifacts should be assessed separately.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive by keeping the old element deprecated while adding the new model. The main tradeoff would be duplicate address-bearing fields and more complicated conformance/search rules.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Organization.address` was a top-level repeating `Address` used for contacting, billing, reporting, and organization disambiguation, and it was directly indexed by the Organization address search parameters. R6 removes that element and places addresses inside `Organization.contact.address`. This preserves the information after a deliberate transform, but a pre-existing R4 instance with a top-level address is old-valid/new-invalid in R6 and generated R6 APIs no longer expose the same property. Because addresses are central organization directory data, the compatibility cost is more than incidental.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Organization.address` is `0..* Address` with requirements for contacting, billing, or reporting.
R6 StructureDefinition: no top-level `Organization.address`; `Organization.contact` is the official contact detail container.
R6 ExtendedContactDetail: `address` is `0..1 Address`; multiple addresses require multiple contact entries.
SearchParameter comparison: R4 address searches point to `Organization.address`; R6 keeps the search codes but expressions point to `Organization.contact.address`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes a direct break to a common administrative/directory path significant, though not as strongly protected as normative content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with top-level `address` fail strict R6 validation unless transformed; generated models and address indexing logic also need path migration.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `Organization.address` as deprecated for one release while adding the richer contact-based representation and requiring search parameters to index both locations. That would preserve most R4 instances but would duplicate address representations and complicate grouping, update semantics, and conflict handling. The tradeoff is material, but the commonness of the field makes the less-breaking option credible.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing high impact and partial-alternative assessment. I agree the consolidation has a coherent goal and non-trivial duplicate-data costs, but I rate the top-level address removal as concerning enough to Revisit.

findings.title: Organization.contact changed from a local backbone component to ExtendedContactDetail, changing codegen and contact.name JSON shape

oldState.summary: R4 `Organization.contact` was a local `BackboneElement` with child elements `purpose`, `name 0..1`, `telecom 0..*`, and `address 0..1`.

semanticText.short: Contact for the organization for a certain purpose
semanticText.definition: Contact for the organization for a certain purpose.
semanticText.comment: Where multiple contacts for the same purpose are provided there is a standard extension that can be used to determine which one is the preferred contact to use.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 generators commonly produce an `OrganizationContactComponent`-style nested class. In JSON, `contact.name` is a single `HumanName` object when present.

newState.summary: R6 `Organization.contact` is typed as `ExtendedContactDetail`; the datatype supplies `purpose`, `name 0..*`, `telecom`, `address`, plus new `organization` and `period` elements.

semanticText.short: Official contact details for the Organization
semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available relevant to the specific Organization. This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.
semanticText.comment: The address/telecom use code 'home' are not to be used. Note that these contacts are not the contact details of people who provide the service (that would be through PractitionerRole), these are official contacts for the Organization itself for specific purposes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 reuses a datatype rather than defining Organization-specific contact children. `ExtendedContactDetail.name` is repeatable, so FHIR JSON represents it as an array.

facts.note: These have no direct R4 Organization.contact equivalents.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same `Organization.contact` path remains, but its type changes from a resource-specific component to `ExtendedContactDetail`; the datatype contains close analogs for the old child elements plus additional fields.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The local element type replacement is a high code generation/API break. It can also be a direct R4-to-R6 wire-format break where R4 data uses `contact.name` as a singleton object; R6 requires the repeating `name` element to be serialized as an array. R6 contact `period` and `organization` create downgrade data-loss risk.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is mostly interoperability/runtime rather than direct safety, but losing named contact context can affect administrative routing and accountability.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Replacing the local backbone with `ExtendedContactDetail` advances a legitimate cross-resource reuse and consistency goal, but it is disruptive for generated models and for `contact.name` serialization. A less-breaking local backbone could represent many of the same facts while preserving R4 instances, yet it would not actually achieve the reusable datatype model and would require duplicate maintenance of similar contact structures. A parallel alias would add even more same-resource duplication. Those tradeoffs support a `Partial` alternative and a probably justified verdict.
justification.inferredGoal: Replace the Organization-specific contact backbone with a reusable extended contact datatype.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 local contact backbone shape and add optional missing context fields, or add a parallel ExtendedContactDetail-based element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained the R4 `Organization.contact` backbone, kept `contact.name` as a singleton, and added optional fields such as contact period or handling organization locally. That would protect old instances and codegen. However, it would forgo the main modeling benefit of a common `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype, or else require a second parallel contact representation and conversion rules between the two.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old JSON/API shape, but either loses the shared datatype goal or creates parallel contact models with mapping ambiguity.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is invalid in R6 specifically because `contact.name` must be an array after the type replacement. The R6 example shows downgrade loss for multiple names, period, and handler organization.

findings.narrativeMd: `Organization.contact` keeps its path but not its model identity. R4 code that references a generated nested contact component, or JSON serializers that emit a single `contact.name` object, need changes. The rest of the old contact fields are recognizable, but they now come from a shared datatype with extra context fields.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 contact entries without `name` may be structurally close to R6, but R4 contact entries with `name` serialized as an object become invalid under R6 JSON rules. R6 instances with more than one contact name, contact validity period, or handler organization cannot be represented cleanly in core R4 Organization without extensions or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models from R6 definitions and update mapping code for `Organization.contact`. Convert singleton `contact.name` objects to one-item arrays. Decide how to downgrade or extend R4 for `ExtendedContactDetail.period` and `ExtendedContactDetail.organization` if bidirectional exchange is required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less disruptive design could have retained the R4 backbone and added new optional children, but that would duplicate the reusable datatype. The chosen design favors consistency across FHIR at the cost of local codegen and JSON compatibility.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding intentionally treats the `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype only as it affects `Organization.contact`. A full datatype-level assessment should be done separately.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `Organization.contact` path remains, but its type changes from an Organization-specific backbone to the reusable `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype. Most familiar child concepts still exist, but generated code changes type names/classes and `contact.name` changes from a singleton `HumanName` in R4 to repeating `HumanName` in R6, which changes FHIR JSON serialization for instances that include a named contact. That is a real API and wire-shape migration burden. The R6 goal of using a shared extended contact datatype is nevertheless a substantive modeling goal rather than a simple rename, and the affected data can generally be transformed without clinical meaning loss.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Organization.contact` is `0..* BackboneElement`.
R4 StructureDefinition: `Organization.contact.name` is `0..1 HumanName`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Organization.contact` is `0..* ExtendedContactDetail`.
R6 ExtendedContactDetail: `name` is `0..* HumanName`, with optional `organization` and `period` context.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means generated API and instance-shape breaks matter, but the resource was still trial-use and the R6 reusable datatype goal reduces the concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated models change from a local backbone component to a datatype; also old-valid/new-invalid for R4 JSON where `contact.name` is serialized as an object instead of the R6 repeating-array shape.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained the local backbone and added optional fields such as period and handling organization, or made the reusable datatype closer to the R4 cardinalities. That would reduce breakage but would undercut cross-resource reuse or force duplicate maintenance of parallel contact structures. The less-breaking designs have enough architectural cost that the break appears proportionate.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree in substance with the existing high impact and partial-alternative assessment: the compatibility burden is real, but the shared datatype objective makes the break probably acceptable.

findings.title: R6 newly forbids home-use telecom and address values inside Organization.contact

oldState.summary: R4 forbade `home` use on top-level `Organization.telecom` and `Organization.address`, but the nested `Organization.contact.telecom` and `Organization.contact.address` elements had no Organization-specific no-home invariant.
oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 contact-party telecom or address with `use = home` was not prohibited by the Organization StructureDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 adds local error constraints on `Organization.contact`: `org-3` requires `telecom.where(use = 'home').empty()` and `org-4` requires `address.where(use = 'home').empty()`.

constraints.human: The telecom of an organization can never be of use 'home'
The address of an organization can never be of use 'home'

newState.narrativeMd: The no-home rule now applies to all R6 official contact entries, including contacts migrated from R4 nested contact details.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 snapshot shows the no-home invariants on removed top-level `telecom` and `address` elements, while R4 nested contact children lack them. The R6 snapshot places the constraints directly on `Organization.contact`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validator break for a narrower instance pattern: an R4 `Organization.contact.telecom` or `Organization.contact.address` with `use = home` can validate in R4 but fail R6 after migration to `Organization.contact`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The business risk is usually low, but automated migrations that preserve `home` can fail validation or silently drop contact-use semantics if not handled deliberately.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The restriction aligns with the R6 definition of `Organization.contact` as official organization contact details rather than personal home contact details. The break is real but narrow: only R4 nested contact telecom/address values using `home` are affected. A warning-first or profile-only path would be less disruptive, but it would not give base R6 consumers a reliable official-only contact invariant, so the stricter base rule is probably justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Ensure organization contact points and addresses are official/business contacts, not home contact details.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a warning/best-practice invariant or profile-level rule before enforcing no-home contact use in the base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have introduced the no-home rule as a warning or best-practice invariant, or left error-level enforcement to profiles that require official-only organization contact data. That would let edge-case R4 instances continue to validate during transition. The tradeoff is that base R6 instances could still carry home-use organization contacts, undermining the semantic cleanup the new contact model appears to seek.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves rare legacy home-use contact data, but weakens the base guarantee that Organization contacts are official/business contacts.

evidence.detail: R4 nested contact telecom has only the inherited `ele-1` constraint, not an Organization no-home constraint.
R4 nested contact address has only the inherited `ele-1` constraint, not an Organization no-home constraint.
R6 adds error constraints forbidding `home` use on contact telecom and address.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows one possible policy (`home` to `work`), but real migrations should not blindly recode use values without business review.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 applies the official-contact no-home rule to the new `Organization.contact` structure. This is not merely carrying forward the old top-level rule: R4 nested contact telecom/address did not have that Organization-specific invariant.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 nested contact details using `home` can become invalid in R6. The issue is validation-time rather than codegen-time, and it is likely less common than top-level telecom/address usage.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan R4 `Organization.contact.telecom.use` and `Organization.contact.address.use` for `home` before migration. Decide whether to omit the use, recode it to an allowed value, move the data to a more appropriate resource, or flag it for manual cleanup.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning-first approach would have been less breaking, but R6 chose a base invariant consistent with the official-organization-contact semantics. The alternative trades strict interoperability for easier migration of edge-case legacy data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 already prohibited `home` use on top-level organization telecom and address, but the nested `Organization.contact.telecom` and `Organization.contact.address` elements did not carry that Organization-specific error invariant. R6 applies no-home error constraints to the new official contact container. This can reject a narrow class of R4 contact entries after migration, especially if an implementation used the nested contact as a person's home contact. The affected pattern is likely uncommon and the R6 rule is aligned with the stated official-organization-contact semantics.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: top-level `Organization.telecom` and `Organization.address` forbid `home`, but nested `Organization.contact.telecom` and `.address` only have inherited element constraints.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Organization.contact` has error constraints `org-3` and `org-4` forbidding `telecom.use = home` and `address.use = home`.
R6 `Organization.contact` comment says these are official contacts for the Organization, not provider-person contact details.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use keeps the validator break relevant, but the break is narrow and reinforces a rule that already applied to R4's official top-level organization contact fields.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 nested contact telecom/address using `home` can become invalid under the R6 Organization contact constraints.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-level invariant or profile-specific rule would be less disruptive for legacy home-use contact data. The tradeoff is that base R6 would continue to permit home contacts in a container explicitly defined as official organization contact information, weakening the cleanup. For this narrow pattern, the stricter base rule appears proportionate.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Agree with the existing medium impact and partial-alternative assessment: there is a real validator break, but it is narrow and the less-breaking warning/profile approach would weaken the R6 semantic guarantee.

findings.title: R6 adds Organization.description, which has no core R4 Organization counterpart

oldState.summary: R4 Organization had no core `description` element.
oldState.narrativeMd: General descriptive/disambiguating text had to be represented through narrative, extensions, aliases, identifiers, or profile-specific rules.

newState.summary: R6 adds `Organization.description` as `0..1 markdown`, included in summaries.

semanticText.short: Additional details about the Organization that could be displayed as further information to identify the Organization beyond its name
semanticText.definition: Description of the organization, which helps provide additional general context on the organization to ensure that the correct organization is selected.
semanticText.requirements: Humans need additional information to verify a correct Organization has been selected.

newState.narrativeMd: The new field is optional for R6 creation and validation, but R6 instances that use it cannot be losslessly downgraded into base R4 Organization.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No R4 local Organization element has the same path or equivalent general description semantics; R6 adds the element directly under Organization.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional R6 element does not invalidate R4 data moving forward, but an R6 instance with `description` cannot be represented in core R4 without an extension or lossy narrative-only mapping.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The field helps humans select the correct organization. Losing it may increase directory disambiguation risk, but it is not usually a direct clinical safety issue.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of adding human-readable disambiguation for organizations is reasonable, and the field is optional, so R4-valid instances are not invalidated by this base R6 design. The compatibility concern is R6-to-R4 downgrade loss when R6 instances use the new field, not R4-to-R6 breakage. That makes the change justified for this calibration purpose.
justification.inferredGoal: Support additional human-readable disambiguation beyond the organization name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed because `Organization.description` is an optional additive R6 element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is `Not applicable` because this finding is an additive optional R6 feature that preserves R4 instances. Representing the value in an R4 extension or narrative can be useful migration guidance for downgrades, but it is not a less-breaking base R6 design alternative under the calibration rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or narrative mappings can mitigate downgrade loss, but they are conversion/backport strategies rather than backward-compatible base R6 alternatives.

r6NotRepresentableInR4Json.name: Acme Health
r6NotRepresentableInR4Json.description: Regional pediatric specialty network, not the similarly named payer.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can preserve this only by agreement, such as an extension or narrative text. A narrative-only downgrade is not a computable round trip.

findings.narrativeMd: `Organization.description` is a useful R6 addition for human disambiguation. The breaking aspect is one-directional: R4 systems receiving downgraded R6 data have no base element to hold the value.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid merely because R6 added this optional field. However, valid R6 content using `description` is not cleanly R4-representable in the core resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 exchange, define an extension mapping or decide whether to copy the text into narrative with known loss of computability. Test downgrade/upgrade cycles to ensure the description is not silently discarded if it is important to directory selection.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding an optional core element is backward-compatible for forward validation, but not for downgrade. An extension-only approach would have preserved R4 compatibility at the expense of weaker standardization.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Organization.description` is an optional R6 addition for human-readable disambiguation. It does not invalidate any R4 Organization instance moving forward. The only concern is downgrade or round-trip loss if an R6 instance using the new markdown field must be represented in core R4 without an extension or narrative convention. That is normal additive-version behavior and does not indicate a problematic R6 base design.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Organization.description` is `0..1 markdown` and helps users verify the correct Organization.
R4 StructureDefinition: no `Organization.description` element exists.
The element is optional, so R4 instances remain valid with respect to this change when moving to R6.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not turn an optional additive R6 field into an R4-to-R6 compatibility break; it only suggests downgrade guidance may be useful.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 description has no core R4 slot, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed. Avoiding the field would reduce R6 expressiveness, while R4 extensions or narrative mappings are downgrade mitigations rather than better R6 base designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Disagree with treating this as medium impact for fresh-review purposes. I agree that downgrade loss exists and that no base-design alternative is needed, but the optional additive nature makes this No problem.

findings.title: R6 adds Organization.qualification, creating substantial R6-to-R4 structured data loss risk

oldState.summary: R4 Organization had no core `qualification` backbone.
oldState.narrativeMd: Licenses, accreditations, certifications, and similar qualifications required extensions, related resources, or profile-specific modeling in R4.

newState.summary: R6 adds `Organization.qualification 0..*` with identifier, mandatory code, status, period, and issuer.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children or both

semanticText.short: Qualifications, certifications, accreditations, licenses, training, etc. pertaining to the provision of care
semanticText.definition: The official certifications, accreditations, training, designations and licenses that authorize and/or otherwise endorse the provision of care by the organization.

newState.narrativeMd: Within each qualification, `code` is required (`1..1 CodeableConcept`), `status` has a preferred `qualification-status` binding, and `issuer` references Organization.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element is newly present as a local Organization backbone; no R4 local element provides a comparable structured qualification container.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because the backbone is optional, but it is a high downgrade and round-trip risk. R6 can carry regulatory or credentialing facts that base R4 cannot preserve without extensions or an alternate resource pattern.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Qualification, accreditation, and license data can affect service eligibility, directory trust, and regulatory workflows. Silent data loss on downgrade can be operationally significant.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Structured organization qualifications, accreditations, licenses, status, period, and issuer are a plausible core R6 need, especially for directory and regulatory workflows. Because the backbone is optional, it does not make R4 Organization instances invalid in R6. The main risk is loss or governance complexity when converting R6 content back to R4, so the change is probably justified while requiring explicit downgrade policy.
justification.inferredGoal: Represent official organization qualifications, certifications, accreditations, licenses, and their status/issuer in core Organization.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed because `Organization.qualification` is an optional additive R6 backbone.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is `Not applicable` for the R4-to-R6 base-design question because this is optional new R6 content. A standard R4 extension, profile, or related-resource mapping may be necessary for round-trip exchange, but those are ordinary R6-to-R4 mitigation/backport mechanisms and should not be counted as a `Yes` or `Partial` base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or related-resource mappings can preserve downgrade round trips, but they are mitigation strategies rather than backward-compatible base R6 alternatives.

evidence.quote: Qualifications, certifications, accreditations, licenses, training, etc. pertaining to the provision of care

evidence.detail: The R6 package contains a complete qualification-status CodeSystem with statuses such as active, inactive, suspended, and revoked.

examples.examplesMd: Base R4 Organization has no structured place for this backbone. Extensions can preserve it, but only if both sides agree on URLs and semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a substantial new qualification model to Organization. This is valuable new expressivity rather than a forward validation break, but it is one of the largest downgrade risks: R4 cannot carry the structured code/status/period/issuer set in the base resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to this optional addition. R6 instances that use `qualification` are not losslessly representable as core R4 Organization instances; the mandatory `qualification.code` also means partial R6 qualification entries cannot be treated as vague notes without changing their meaning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 exchange, define a standard extension mapping, an implementation-guide-specific profile, or a related-resource strategy. Treat qualification status codes as terminology-bearing data and test active/inactive/revoked cases. Avoid silently flattening qualifications into narrative if downstream systems make eligibility or credentialing decisions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An extension-first path would have been more R4-compatible but less visible in the core R6 model. Given the regulatory and directory significance of qualifications, adding a core backbone is plausible, but cross-version implementers need explicit mapping policy.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology expansion for the qualification code itself was not available because `qualification.code` has an example binding without a valueSet. Human review is recommended for jurisdiction-specific accreditation and licensure mappings.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Organization.qualification` is an optional R6 backbone for certifications, accreditations, licenses, status, period, and issuer. It is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but an R6 Organization that relies on this structured data cannot be faithfully downgraded into core R4 without extensions or another agreed mapping. Because qualification and accreditation data can matter for directory trust, eligibility, and regulatory workflows, that reverse-conversion loss is meaningful. Still, adding optional structured qualification data is a reasonable R6 evolution, and a more backward-compatible base design would mostly mean not adding the needed R6 capability.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Organization.qualification` is `0..* BackboneElement` for qualifications, certifications, accreditations, licenses, and training.
R6 StructureDefinition: `qualification.code` is required `1..1 CodeableConcept`; optional fields include status, period, and issuer.
R6 CodeSystem `qualification-status` includes active, inactive, suspended, revoked, and related lifecycle statuses.
R4 StructureDefinition: no core `Organization.qualification` path exists.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use supports taking reverse-conversion loss seriously where regulatory or directory-trust data is involved, but it does not make an optional additive R6 backbone a forward hard break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: structured R6 qualification/accreditation data has no core R4 representation, so downgrade requires extensions, alternate resources, or lossy omission.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: There is no attractive less-breaking R6 base design for the R4-to-R6 direction because the element is optional and additive. Deferring the content to extensions would preserve R4 core symmetry but would sacrifice the R6 goal of a standard structured slot for organization qualifications. Downgrade mappings are mitigation, not a better base R6 design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing high downgrade-risk assessment and not-applicable alternative judgment. I agree the reverse loss can be important, but judge the optional additive R6 design as proportionate rather than a reason to Revisit.

`Organization.type` remains example-bound to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/organization-type` with the same compose system. Contact-purpose binding is weakened as part of the contact remodel; full terminology expansions were not available.
